1.w: A well-written song by Asaph. Pay attention, my people, to my instruction. Listen to the words I speak.

2.w: I will sing a song that imparts wisdom; I will make insightful observations about the past.

3.w: What we have heard and learned — that which our ancestors have told us—

4.w: we will not hide from their descendants. We will tell the next generation about the Lord’s praiseworthy acts, about his strength and the amazing things he has done.

5.w: He established a rule in Jacob; he set up a law in Israel. He commanded our ancestors to make his deeds known to their descendants,

6.w: so that the next generation, children yet to be born, might know about them. They will grow up and tell their descendants about them.

7.w: Then they will place their confidence in God. They will not forget the works of God, and they will obey his commands.

8.w: Then they will not be like their ancestors, who were a stubborn and rebellious generation, a generation that was not committed and faithful to God.

9.w: The Ephraimites were armed with bows, but they retreated in the day of battle.

10.w: They did not keep their covenant with God, and they refused to obey his law.

11.w: They forgot what he had done, the amazing things he had shown them.

12.w: He did amazing things in the sight of their ancestors, in the land of Egypt, in the region of Zoan.

13.w: He divided the sea and led them across it; he made the water stand in a heap.

14.w: He led them with a cloud by day and with the light of a fire all night long.

15.w: He broke open rocks in the wilderness and gave them enough water to fill the depths of the sea.

16.w: He caused streams to flow from the rock and made the water flow like rivers.

17.w: Yet they continued to sin against him and rebelled against the Most High in the desert.

18.w: They willfully challenged God by asking for food to satisfy their appetite.

19.w: They insulted God, saying, “Is God really able to give us food in the wilderness?

20.w: Yes, he struck a rock and water flowed out; streams gushed forth. But can he also give us food? Will he provide meat for his people?”

21.w: When the Lord heard this, he was furious. A fire broke out against Jacob, and his anger flared up against Israel,

22.w: because they did not have faith in God and did not trust his ability to deliver them.

23.w: He gave a command to the clouds above and opened the doors in the sky.

24.w: He rained down manna for them to eat; he gave them the grain of heaven.

25.w: Man ate the food of the mighty ones. He sent them more than enough to eat.

26.w: He brought the east wind through the sky and by his strength led forth the south wind.

27.w: He rained down meat on them like dust, birds as numerous as the sand on the seashores.

28.w: He caused them to fall right in the middle of their camp, all around their homes.

29.w: They ate until they were beyond full; he gave them what they desired.

30.w: They were not yet filled up; their food was still in their mouths

31.w: when the anger of God flared up against them. He killed some of the strongest of them; he brought the young men of Israel to their knees.

32.w: Despite all this, they continued to sin, and did not trust him to do amazing things.

33.w: So he caused them to die unsatisfied and filled with terror.

34.w: When he struck them down, they sought his favor; they turned back and longed for God.

35.w: They remembered that God was their protector and that God Most High was their deliverer.

36.w: But they deceived him with their words and lied to him.

37.w: They were not really committed to him, and they were unfaithful to his covenant.

38.w: Yet he is compassionate. He forgives sin and does not destroy. He often holds back his anger and does not stir up his fury.

39.w: He remembered that they were made of flesh and were like a wind that blows past and does not return.

40.w: How often they rebelled against him in the wilderness and insulted him in the wastelands.

41.w: They again challenged God and offended the Holy One of Israel.

42.w: They did not remember what he had done, how he delivered them from the enemy,

43.w: when he performed his awesome deeds in Egypt and his acts of judgment in the region of Zoan.

44.w: He turned their rivers into blood, and they could not drink from their streams.

45.w: He sent swarms of biting insects against them, as well as frogs that overran their land.

46.w: He gave their crops to the grasshopper, the fruit of their labor to the locust.

47.w: He destroyed their vines with hail and their sycamore-fig trees with driving rain.

48.w: He rained hail down on their cattle and hurled lightning bolts down on their livestock.

49.w: His raging anger lashed out against them. He sent fury, rage, and trouble as messengers who bring disaster.

50.w: He sent his anger in full force. He did not spare them from death; he handed their lives over to destruction.

51.w: He struck down all the firstborn in Egypt, the firstfruits of their reproductive power in the tents of Ham.

52.w: Yet he brought out his people like sheep; he led them through the wilderness like a flock.

53.w: He guided them safely along, and they were not afraid; but the sea covered their enemies.

54.w: He brought them to the border of his holy land, to this mountainous land that his right hand acquired.

55.w: He drove the nations out from before them; he assigned them their tribal allotments and allowed the tribes of Israel to settle down.

56.w: Yet they challenged and defied God Most High and did not obey his commands.

57.w: They were unfaithful and acted as treacherously as their ancestors; they were as unreliable as a malfunctioning bow.

58.w: They made him angry with their pagan shrines and made him jealous with their idols.

59.w: God heard and was angry; he completely rejected Israel.

60.w: He abandoned the sanctuary at Shiloh, the tent where he lived among men.

61.w: He allowed the symbol of his strong presence to be captured; he gave the symbol of his splendor into the hand of the enemy.

62.w: He delivered his people over to the sword and was angry with his chosen nation.

63.w: Fire consumed their young men, and their virgins remained unmarried.

64.w: Their priests fell by the sword, but their widows did not weep.

65.w: But then the Lord awoke from his sleep; he was like a warrior in a drunken rage.

66.w: He drove his enemies back; he made them a permanent target for insults.

67.w: He rejected the tent of Joseph; he did not choose the tribe of Ephraim.

68.w: He chose the tribe of Judah and Mount Zion, which he loves.

69.w: He made his sanctuary as enduring as the heavens above, as secure as the earth, which he established permanently.

70.w: He chose David, his servant, and took him from the sheepfolds.

71.w: He took him away from following the mother sheep, and made him the shepherd of Jacob, his people, and of Israel, his chosen nation.

72.w: David cared for them with pure motives; he led them with skill.
